newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS -flat, looking ahead to NJ sale.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS -flat, looking ahead to NJ sale.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were unchanged in early trading on Friday as players anticipated a quiet session as they looked ahead to New Jersey's huge taxable pension obligation bond sale.
The state's Economic Development Authority plans to sell next week $2.75 billion of pension obligation bonds through Merrill Lynch & Co.

The taxable sale was expected to be the first of several possible such pension bond sales, as states look likely to tackle various issues--from capturing a windfall like New Jersey to giving state workers the option of switching to a different type of plan, like Michigan--with such sales.

"It's definitely an opportunity, I see the market going in the direction of taxables (like that)," a trader said. He added that New Jersey's offering could draw crossover interest from corporate bond funds, as well as insurance companies.
The sale by New Jersey accounts for nearly half the new supply anticipated next week.

Other negotiated offerings scheduled included a $233 million sale of revenue bonds by Philadelphia International Airport through Lehman Brothers and a $220 million sale of revenues by the Delaware Valley Regional Finance, through a syndicate led by Merrill.
On the competitive side, Massachusetts planned a $300 million General Obligation bond sale on June 24, which also was the day that Gwinett County Water & Sewer, Georgia, set a $100 million sale.
In early trade on Friday, Georgia Housing/Finance Authority sold $30 million of bonds that were priced at a top yield of 5.85 percent in 2028.
A trader speculated that municipal bonds in the secondary market might erode by one-eighth to a quarter of a point on Friday, mainly due to the lackluster interest ahead of a summer weekend.
The market next week will get several key economic reports, including durable goods for May on June 25, and the First Quarter Gross Domestic Product data on June 27.

Towards the end of the week, however, traders said activity might slow ahead of the Federal Reserve policy makers meeting, which is set for early July. While the market appeared confident that the central bank would not tighten monetary policy, it still was wary.
"It's coming up, it's going to be on people's minds," a trader said.

September U.S. Treasury bond futures on the Chicago Board of Trade firmed three ticks to 112-9/32, while the September municipal bond futures fell seven ticks to 118-5/32. The MOB spread stood at 188 ticks, down 11 ticks from late Thursday.

In the secondary market, actively quoted issues included Cleveland, Ohio, Certificates of Participation Cleveland Stadium Project of 2027, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, and were bid at 5.54 percent, down one basis point.
And Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority of 2023, which carry a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.49 percent, down one basis point.
